messages:
anna (CS): FYI ACME reported a 403 on /v1/generate, only sent a screenshot — no request id in response. Can SRE/eng confirm what to ask for? :wave:

mike (SRE): Ask them for a HAR from Chrome or a curl with -i so we can see response headers. Common header names to look for: X-Req-Ref, X-Request-Id, x-redwood-request-id. Also ask for the approximate client timestamp (UTC) when the failure happened. :mag:

anna (CS): Sent this to the customer (copying here so eng can review):
> Hi — thanks for the report. Could you please: 1) capture a HAR (Chrome DevTools Network -> right-click -> Save all as HAR) from the failing request; 2) OR run a curl with -i to capture response headers and paste the full output (please redact the Authorization token); 3) if you use our SDK, include 5–10 lines of SDK logs around the failure (look for strings like `correlation_id` or `session_hash`); 4) include your local time (with timezone) when the error happened. Example curl below.

jay (runtime): Example curl we can ask them to run (remind to redact tokens):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

mike (SRE): If they provide a HAR we typically extract the header value with jq like: 
```
jq -r '.log.entries[].response.headers[] | select(.name=="X-Req-Ref") .value' file.har
```
This will quickly show any request-id the edge returned. If the header is missing, the curl -i output helps us confirm.

anna (CS): Mobile customers often struggle with HARs — what are our quick mobile asks?

jay (runtime): Android: ask them to capture Logcat around the failure and grep for `RedwoodClient` or `correlation_id=` with the timestamp. Example:
```
adb logcat | grep RedwoodClient
# look for lines like: RedwoodClient: request failed correlation_id=abcd1234
```

jay (runtime): iOS: ask for the device logs from Xcode (Devices & Simulators -> View Device Logs) and check for `session_hash` or `x-req-ref` entries; if they can produce a sysdiagnose / network capture that's helpful.

mike (SRE): If the customer is on Dedicated or Private and they claim headers are stripped, ask for their proxy/nginx access logs and the client timestamp — we can match by path and time. Also ask them to generate a debug bundle from the Console: Settings -> Support -> Generate debug bundle (attach the ZIP). That bundle often contains the edge logs and routing metadata we need.

anna (CS): If they only send a screenshot I'll escalate but request we include the screenshot, the local time, and any available 20 lines of customer logs we have. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Escalation created: #INC-2026-1234 — assigned to mike (SRE).

mike (SRE): Once we have the req-ref or correlation id we'll grep internal logs, e.g.:
```
grep -R "abcd1234" /var/log/redwood/* | head
```
That lets us find the service span and correlate to edge logs.

anna (CS): Thanks — I'll update the thread when the customer returns HAR or curl output.
